The relation of “jihad” is with this second meaning, that is, with the removal of the social and political wrongdoing and corruption established in a society, not with the spiritual station of taqwā of the prophets. Therefore jihad is against that wrongdoing which, in the form of fasād fī al-arḍ, erases social justice.

### 1. The End of Wrongdoing and Corruption

The fundamental purpose of jihad is the protection of the oppressed and the ending of corruption. Allah the Exalted says:

>> وَقَٰتِلُوهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ لَا تَكُونَ فِتۡنَةٞ وَيَكُونَ ٱلدِّينُ لِلَّهِۖ فَإِنِ ٱنتَهَوۡاْ فَلَا عُدۡوَٰنَ إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ

*“Fight them until there is no [more] fitnah and [until] worship is [acknowledged to be] for Allah. But if they cease, then there is to be no aggression except against the oppressors”* (Sūrat al-Baqarah 2:193 · trans. Sahih International)

**Explanation:** The aim of jihad is to uproot fitnah and corruption from society. The incident of Dhū al-Qarnayn (Sūrat al-Kahf: 93–94) is the best example of this. He built a wall against the corruption of Yājūj and Mājūj, which was a state action of “stopping corruption by force”.

### 2. The Declaration of Jihad: A Duty of the State and of Society

According to Islamic law, the regular declaration of jihad is the right only of the state or of the established social authority (State Authority), not of individuals. Allah the Exalted says in the wise Qur’an:

>> يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱلرَّسُولَ وَأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِ مِنكُمۡۖ فَإِن تَنَٰزَعۡتُمۡ فِي شَيۡءٖ فَرُدُّوهُ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِ إِن كُنتُمۡ تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ ذَٰلِكَ خَيۡرٞ وَأَحۡسَنُ تَأۡوِيلًا

*“O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is the best [way] and best in result”* (Sūrat al-Nisāʾ 4:59 · trans. Sahih International)

**Explanation:** In the light of this verse, deciding war policy, defence policy and matters of foreign affairs is the responsibility of the state. If individuals themselves begin to declare jihad, the danger arises of social anarchy and disorder, and avoiding this is a demand of the sharīʿah.

### 3. The Individual’s Role: An Effective Voice against Wrongdoing

As members of the ummah, raising one’s voice against wrongdoing and barbarity is the religious and moral duty of every individual. Allah the Exalted says:

>> كُنتُمۡ خَيۡرَ أُمَّةٍ أُخۡرِجَتۡ لِلنَّاسِ تَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِ وَتَنۡهَوۡنَ عَنِ ٱلۡمُنكَرِ وَتُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِۗ وَلَوۡ ءَامَنَ أَهۡلُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَكَانَ خَيۡرٗا لَّهُمۚ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَأَكۡثَرُهُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ

*“You are the best nation produced [as an example] for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah. If only the People of the Scripture had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient”* (Sūrat Āl ʿImrān 3:110 · trans. Sahih International)

**Explanation:** In this context, according to the teachings of the Prophet ﷺ, “stopping evil by the hand” does not mean armed struggle. It means peaceful protest, diplomatic pressure, and moral and financial assistance to the oppressed, according to one’s capacity. This action is a means of individual awakening and social reform, which is based on constructive struggle, not on self-made militancy.

### 4. The State’s Responsibility and the Establishment of Justice

It is the duty of the state to maintain justice even toward the enemy:

>> يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّـٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ وَلَا يَجۡرِمَنَّكُمۡ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوۡمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعۡدِلُواْۚ ٱعۡدِلُواْ هُوَ أَقۡرَبُ لِلتَّقۡوَىٰۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرُۢ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ

*“O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do”* (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:8 · trans. Sahih International)

**Explanation:** If the state is not fulfilling its responsibility, then the task of the public is to put pressure on the government, through lawful means and peaceful protest, so that it corrects its policy.

### 5. The Nation State and International Treaties

In the present age the “nation state” system is a reality, and Islam does not reject this system. It sees it as a platform for establishing justice and fairness. Adherence to international treaties in the nation state system is not merely a political necessity. It is a religious obligation. Allah the Exalted says:

>> يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ أَوۡفُواْ بِٱلۡعُقُودِۚ أُحِلَّتۡ لَكُم بَهِيمَةُ ٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ إِلَّا مَا يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡكُمۡ غَيۡرَ مُحِلِّي ٱلصَّيۡدِ وَأَنتُمۡ حُرُمٌۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَحۡكُمُ مَا يُرِيدُ

*“O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts. Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock except for that which is recited to you [in this Qur'an] - hunting not being permitted while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah ordains what He intends”* (Sūrat al-Māʾidah 5:1 · trans. Sahih International)

In this connection it is necessary to understand that the concept of jihad, which is a state’s regular army taking action for its own defence or for the help of the oppressed, now remains within the scope of these international laws and treaties of the state. This system rejects individual militancy, and stresses that the decisions of war and peace are the right of the state alone, so that social peace may remain. Therefore a Muslim state’s adherence to its treaties is in reality the practical picture of Islamic principles (fulfilment of the covenant), which at the global level reflects the responsible and peaceful identity of Islam.
